Budd-Chiari syndrome: The patient presents with hepatomegaly, ascites, and hepatic vein thrombosis, which are characteristic findings of Budd-Chiari syndrome. The presence of thrombosis in the hepatic veins and the inferior vena cava, as well as the reversal of portal venous flow, further supports this diagnosis.
Hepatorenal syndrome: The patient developed hepatorenal syndrome, as evidenced by the rapid progression of renal failure in the setting of liver disease. The presence of ascites, hepatic vein thrombosis, and renal failure supports this diagnosis.
